spoken: I am still floating! We went into Barcelona six points behind, under massive pressure, and pulled off a 2-1 victory! Mbappé opened it in the 41st minute, Raphinha equalised in the 61st, and then Mbappé again off Eduardo Camavinga's assist in the 87th minute!
Exactly when Jose Mourinho needed it. That cuts the gap at the top to three points.
Where does that leave us in the standings?
Barcelona stay top on 27 points. Atlético Madrid are second with 25, Real Madrid move to third with 24 points, and Real Betis are fourth on 20.
That changes the whole mood around Madrid!

Although former Madrid keeper Santi Canizares raised questions on COPE about the Mbappé and Vinicius Jr partnership. He argued their lack of defensive work leaves Bellingham working twice as much and leaves the team disconnected up front.
Canizares can say what he wants, Mbappé reached 100 goals for Real Madrid! In just 116 appearances!

He is the second-fastest to a hundred goals for Madrid in the 21st century, behind only Cristiano Ronaldo's 105 matches. Sixty-seven in La Liga, 25 in the Champions League, four in Copa del Rey, two in the Club World Cup, one in the UEFA Super Cup, and one in the Spanish Super Cup.
Unbelievable! But did you see Guti hitting out at Harry Kane winning the Ballon d'Or in London over Lamine Yamal and Mbappé? He called it orchestrated!
Kane scored 73 goals for club and country, so Thomas Tuchel certainly felt it was deserved. Even Virat Kohli congratulated Kane on X, praising his resilience and hard work.
Speaking of cricket, how about Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashing 100 in five overs?
That set a new world record for the fastest team hundred in men's T20Is. They equalled the fastest fifty in 2.2 overs and got the highest total in the first six overs.
Pure carnage at the top!
Out in Wellington, Daryl Mitchell hit a 52-ball 89 to push New Zealand to 198 for 3 in the third T20I. India's bowlers did well at the finish though, giving away just 52 runs in the last five overs.
Now, Formula 1 at Austin... Max Verstappen finished third from second on the grid behind winner Antonelli and Leclerc.
That P3 mathematically ends Max's title hopes. It ends a streak of 2,184 days where he was in contention for the world championship, going back to 2020.
Six years! Four titles in between! But the team radio failed him again!
He was furious. He joked they should start communicating in sign language because the Red Bull radio keeps dropping out.
And Isack Hadjar finished sixth after clutch troubles off the line and a bad engine map that limited his throttle.

In tennis, Carlos Alcaraz faces Karen Khachanov today in Vienna. He is also set to lead Spain's Davis Cup Finals team in Bologna alongside Rafael Jodar, Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, Marcel Granollers, and Pedro Martinez.
Who is in the Germany squad?
Alexander Zverev, Jan-Lennard Struff, Kevin Krawietz, and Tim Puetz. Ben Shelton mentioned recently that it was sad for tennis to have Alcaraz and Sinner miss so much of the year due to injuries.
Time for Rival Watch! Barcelona had nine wins from nine in the league, talking about running away with La Liga! Then Mourinho brings Real Madrid to town and hands them a 2-1 defeat on their own turf!
Raphinha scored, but Mbappé's double broke their perfect domestic start. A satisfying slip for them.
The Warriors finally got a win! 134-114 over Denver!

After three straight losses, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg exploded for 31 points and 12 rebounds. Steph Curry had a solid game, Al Horford added 11 off the bench hitting 3-for-3 from deep, and Golden State shot 54 percent from the field to avoid an 0-4 start. Nikola Jokic had 19 points before sitting out.
Did you hear about Alex Albon and Fernando Alonso clashing at Austin?
Alonso took a jab at the quality at the back of the grid after their Turn 11 collision. Albon replied that it was like watching a Mustang race a Mini at Goodwood.
And Toto Wolff spoke out on George Russell?
Yes, Wolff defended Russell, saying he is a champion who struggles when the car drops out of its operating window.
Any update on Jannik Sinner?

Sinner is returning at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh this December after his knee injury. Also, over 150 men's doubles players signed an open letter protesting the ATP's proposed draw and prize money cuts for 2028.
And Chennai Super Kings named Albie Morkel and Gareth Batty as assistant coaches for IPL 2027! Welcome back, Albie!

spoken: Carlos Alcaraz claimed his seventh win against Karen Khachanov! A 6-4, 7-6 victory to open his Erste Bank Open campaign.

He had to sweat for it, didn't he? It was his first appearance in Vienna since 2021. After being sidelined from April to August with that wrist injury, he needed a solid display after his Shanghai exit.

And did you hear what happened in practice before the tournament? Andrey Rublev beat him 6-2! Carlos said Rublev was straight-up unplayable, hitting every forehand full out. But Carlos stayed calm because he knew his own game was in the right place.

Ben Shelton actually defended Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner this week. People questioned if their dominance was fading. Shelton called that unfair, noting Sinner is out with a knee injury targeting a 2027 return and Alcaraz is working his way back. Sinner also reflected on their rivalry recently, recalling how they split nine straight Majors between early 2024 and 2026. Alcaraz holds a 10-7 head-to-head edge, though Sinner won their last two meetings.
Now, Wellington! What an absolute masterclass by India!
Chasing 199 against New Zealand, and finishing it in 13.2 overs?

199 in 13.2 overs! India won by six wickets to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series. Abhishek Sharma was pure lightning! 113 off just 38 balls, hitting 11 sixes! He took 26 runs off Jacob Duffy in the very first over!
That brought his 2026 tally to 85 sixes, breaking Rohit Sharma's world record of 80 in a calendar year for a Full Member batter. He reached his fifty in 15 balls and his hundred in 35.
And what about fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi? Smashing 45 off 19! Abhishek revealed that Vaibhav promised in the nets he would play fearlessly, quoting Bhaag Milkha Bhaag!
Did Yuvraj Singh say something to Abhishek after the match?
Yuvraj teased him about not hitting a 12-ball fifty like he did in 2007! Abhishek laughed and said scoring fifty off 12 balls isn't easy at all and just happens once in a while.

On the bowling side, Bhuvneshwar Kumar spoke after sealing the series lead. At 36, after four years out, he credited his past two IPL seasons with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, where he took 17 and 28 wickets, for getting him back. He said he never chased the comeback, just kept playing.

Off the field, Cricket Australia posted record revenue of 601.1 million Australian dollars for 2025-26, thanks to broadcast deals for the Ashes and the India white-ball series. But those two two-day Ashes Tests cost them 20 million dollars!
Over to Real Madrid, where Kylian Mbappe is in hot water.
What happened with Mbappe?

He apologized on Tuesday after mentioning a meme of former Chinese leader Mao Zedong on the talk show The Bridge. He called it a dictator meme that made him laugh, playing on how fans call him a dictator.

Chinese sponsors Dongpeng Beverage, Mengniu, and Milkground terminated their deals with him immediately. That threatens his 30 million euro annual sponsor income, and since Madrid holds a share of his image rights, the club loses money too! Plus, Chinese state TV suspended LALIGA broadcasts!

After the Clasico victory, reports are highlighting Yan Diomande. The Ivory Coast winger tormented the defense all night and helped Marc Cucurella defend Lamine Yamal. Some reports are asking if Vinicius Junior should still be a guaranteed starter.
What was that madness with Red Bull radio in Austin?

Isack Hadjar initially refused a team order to let Max Verstappen pass on Lap 13. Hadjar radioed that he didn't want to lose race time, but engineer Richard Wood insisted. Hadjar let Max through at Turn 15. Max finished third, Hadjar sixth. David Coulthard reminded everyone about the rules of engagement.
And what were those strange rumours about Aston Martin and Red Bull?
Mike Krack and Laurent Mekies were asked in the paddock if their teams might partner up. It all came from an F1 Q and A column interpreting customer interest in the Red Bull Ford engine.
At least Jos Verstappen cleared up those scary health rumours online! Someone posted an AI-generated photo of him looking ill. Jos posted a real picture saying he's fine, just having a bad hair day!
Time for Rival Watch. Barcelona were hit with a 602 euro fine by LALIGA for approaching Julian Alvarez without written notice to Atletico.

And Lamine Yamal posted on Instagram after missing out on the Ballon d'Or, saying good things take time! Spain coach Luis de la Fuente backed him to win multiple Ballon d'Ors in his career, while defender Pau Cubarsi is set to receive the Golden Boy award on December 14.
Novak Djokovic praised Serbian students after the Student List won 140 of 250 seats in the parliamentary elections, ending the incumbent government.
Golden State rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has everyone talking after his performance against Denver. He even asked Carmelo Anthony, Tracy McGrady, and Vince Carter for advice live on TV postgame!
Over in Portugal, Cristiano Ronaldo was named in the preliminary squad for next month's Nations League, despite his earlier dispute with coach Jorge Jesus.
In Formula 1, Valtteri Bottas admitted anything can happen regarding his Cadillac seat for 2027, as team boss Marcin Budkowski remains non-committal.
And the FIA signed a deal with AWS to use AI and cloud simulations to improve aerodynamic rules and build better concept cars.

In football, UEFA banned RC Lens fans from buying tickets for their next two Champions League away matches at Leipzig and Liverpool after fans threw flares at Club Brugge supporters. Lens were also fined 80,000 euros!

spoken: We start with Real Madrid, and it is an uncomfortable situation off the pitch. Kylian Mbappé’s comments about an internet meme showing his face on Mao Zedong have caused a massive reaction in China.

How does an internet meme end up causing a diplomatic broadcast dispute like this? Mbappé apologized in Chinese, French, and English, and Madrid put out an official statement expressing regret and respect for China and its people. But China Media rejected it.
The state broadcaster stopped La Liga coverage, pulled promotional content with Mbappé, and insists the club must accept responsibility. It is turning into a serious commercial issue.
It really is. In the paddock, Sergio Perez has signed an extension with Cadillac through 2029.

He becomes only the seventh driver in F1 history to reach 300 race starts this weekend in Mexico. Cadillac have zero points this season, with Lance Stroll the only other driver without a point, but they are backing Perez for the long haul.
Building a new team takes patience. Over in cricket, did you see what Waqar Younis said about Jasprit Bumrah?

On the Shubhankar Mishra podcast, Waqar called Bumrah the standout modern white-ball bowler, but argued he still has a lot to prove in Test cricket because he has not played as much red-ball cricket as Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, or the English pacers.

Is Waqar being fair to Jasprit Bumrah here? Two hundred and thirty-four wickets in fifty-two Tests, averaging under twenty, and strike rate under forty-three! He was the fastest Indian pacer to fifty Test wickets back in 2018.

The numbers are elite. With the Indian white-ball setup preparing for the ODIs, Shubman Gill was seen wearing a temple fitness tracker on his forehead at training, talking with Abhishek Sharma. KL Rahul and pacer Gurnoor Brar have joined the squad, while Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli will return for the ODIs.

And Abhishek Sharma is back to world number one in the ICC T20I batting rankings! Eight hundred and ninety-seven points, overtaking Ishan Kishan, who slipped to third after missing matches through injury. Sahibzada Farhan sits second.

That hundred in Wellington sealed it. Tilak Varma also spoke about adapting to batting at number six after Ishan's injury shuffled Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to three. Tilak said he now takes his time to build before hitting out late.

That fifty in Christchurch showed real maturity. Over in Formula One, Daniel Ricciardo reflected on his exit after Singapore in 2024. He admitted being cut was humiliating at the time, but called it a blessing in hindsight.

Three top-ten finishes in eighteen starts was not what Red Bull wanted when testing him against Sergio Perez. Looking to this weekend, Max Verstappen will sit out first practice in Mexico City to fulfill rookie requirements. Ayumu Iwasa steps in for his eighth FP1 appearance.

In tennis, Stan Wawrinka played his final match in Basel, losing to Jiri Lehecka. Carlos Alcaraz posted a tribute thanking him for checking in during injury recovery earlier this year. Though Carlos did say the match music in Vienna is a little too loud!
Even with the loud arena, he loved the crowd. And Juan Carlos Ferrero told El Mundo he would change things about Carlos's career, admitting he wished he could have continued coaching him.
Now to Novak Djokovic in Basel. What an opening battle.

Did you really think Novak was going to drop his opening match in Basel? He lost the opening set 4-6 to Ugo Humbert, then found his rhythm to take the next two 6-3, 6-4. His first time playing in Basel since 2011.
Thirty-nine years old and still finding solutions when he is under siege. That keeps his push for a nineteenth ATP Finals qualification alive, right after winning his 102nd title in Beijing.
Before the tournament, Novak spoke about Roger Federer, explaining that their relationship across fifty matches was almost always strictly professional.
Honest from him. And Indian billiards icon Pankaj Advani, who just won his 29th world title in Birmingham at 41, pointed directly to Djokovic's longevity and consistency as his inspiration.
Two veterans defying age. Speaking of which, Stephen Curry turned in a ridiculous performance against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Can you believe Steph Curry is still pulling off these nights at thirty-seven? Forty-four points, nineteen in the second quarter, six triples, and a perfect sixteen of sixteen from the free-throw line. Golden State won 119 to 114 on the road.
That ties LeBron James for the most forty-point games after turning 35 in NBA history, with fifteen. Kevin Durant has nine, James Harden six.
Graham Ike started, and the Warriors are taking a strict no-excuses approach after going 37-45 last season, even with Kristaps Porzingis away dealing with health issues.
A complete change in mindset. In football, Cristiano Ronaldo earned another recognition from supporters.

France Football ran a 70th-anniversary fan poll for the greatest Ballon d'Or campaign in history. Cristiano's 2008 run with Manchester United took first place, beating Lionel Messi's 2012 season. No physical trophy, but pure respect from the fans.

And ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix, Pirelli announced the tyre selection: C3 hard, C4 medium, and C5 soft. Drivers get two sets of hards, three mediums, and eight softs, tackling a largely resurfaced track.

Formula One also published its first Social Impact Report. Over half a million young people involved across 71 countries, and they renewed their Engineering Scholarship with over 2.4 million pounds in funding through 2029 for ten new scholars each year.
Around the grounds, Serie A gave us two major upsets.
Bologna went away to AC Milan and stunned them 4-2!
And Genoa took down Juventus 2-0 at home.

spoken: Dhruv, what a performance in Vienna! Alcaraz took Medvedev down 6-4, 7-6. That second-set tiebreak was absolute domination at 7-2.

He got the break in game four, handed it straight back, then stayed composed. Medvedev double-faulted at 5-4 down to give Alcaraz the opening set. That secures Alcaraz a place in his fifth final of the year. Did you track his run earlier in the week?
Every minute. He had that wild 13-11 tiebreak against Nikoloz Basilashvili in a 6-1, 7-6 win, and then held off Tommy Paul 6-4, 7-6. Now he gets Alex de Minaur for the title.
Medvedev did not leave empty-handed either. Making the last four booked his spot for the ATP Finals in Turin. Now, out in New Zealand, the T20 series wrapped up with a thud in Hamilton.
A seven-wicket defeat stings, even if India won the series 3-2. Tim Seifert went berserk with 93 off 50 deliveries. How does our attack fail to defend 192 and let it go with two whole overs left?

Glenn Phillips took them apart at the death. His unbeaten 65 carried him to 341 runs across the series. That breaks Phil Salt's world record from 2023 for the most runs in any bilateral T20 series. India still set up a competitive 191 for eight first.

Ishan Kishan looked outstanding. Sixty-one off 32 balls with five sixes and five fours. That pushed him past Suryakumar Yadav's Indian record for the most T20 international runs in a single calendar year, getting to 1,220 runs. Plus he crossed the 2,000 career run mark in the format.

India also became the first team to reach 400 T20 international sixes in a single calendar year, clearing the rope 11 times. But Gautam Gambhir faced sharp scrutiny after leaving 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi out for the fourth and fifth games.
Why bench the kid right after he hammered 45 off 19 balls?

Gambhir said directly that his job is to make the right decisions, not popular ones, stressing dressing-room security and continuity. Over in Mong Kok at the Hong Kong Sixes, India had a miserable run.

Nightmare stuff. Pakistan beat us by four wickets, then the UAE walked all over us by six wickets. We ended up in the 11th-place bowl play-off beating Bangladesh by five wickets just to finish 11th. Grim reading.

Over in Madrid, alarming news for Eder Militao. Thieves broke into his house through a third-floor bathroom window during the match against Barcelona, stealing watches, bags, and jewellery worth 391,000 dollars.
His family was on the ground floor watching the match! Horrifying to think what could have happened. What is Jose Mourinho planning on the pitch for Racing Santander?

Mourinho looks set to lock in his midfield balance, pairing Bernardo Silva and Aurelien Tchouameni as the double pivot. Tchouameni handles the defensive ball-winning while Bernardo provides the composure to advance play.
Did Mourinho have anything to say about the Kylian Mbappe China controversy?

He said often the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, but praised Mbappe for acting with class by apologizing quickly over his Mao Zedong comments. Off the pitch, Madrid feel confident of completing a January swoop for 16-year-old Manchester United talent JJ Gabriel, whose representatives are seeking an exit from England.
Now, Mexico City. Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson banging wheels in second practice was total madness. That stadium complex scrap was ridiculous.

Verstappen damaged his bargeboards through Turns 12 to 14. He called Lawson's defense not very smart behavior, asking why he would pick a fight with him. The stewards found their actions unacceptable and gave both drivers a one-place grid penalty.

What about qualifying, though? Lewis Hamilton grabbed his first Ferrari pole position! His first pole anywhere since the 2023 Hungarian Grand Prix, beating George Russell by nine thousandths of a second.

At 41, Hamilton becomes the oldest polesitter since Mario Andretti at the 1982 Italian GP. Still in Mexico, Red Bull reserve Isack Hadjar was handed a formal warning for misconduct by the stewards after pushing an aggressive paddock guest seeking a selfie before opening practice.
Then in Basel, what happened to Novak Djokovic?

Jan-Lennard Struff snapped an eight-match losing slide against Djokovic, beating him 6-7, 7-5, 7-6 in the second round. Djokovic admitted the loss hurt, calling Struff's attacking precision something he had rarely faced. Struff then lost his semi-final to Jiri Lehecka, who now plays Valentin Vacherot in the Basel final.
And in Vienna, Alex de Minaur took down incoming world number one Alexander Zverev 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 to book his clash with Alcaraz.

In the NBA, the Golden State Warriors beat the Los Angeles Lakers 112-95. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg struggled badly after his war of words with Luka Doncic, logging six points, five turnovers, and fouling out at minus-20, but the team bailed him out. Steph Curry and Draymond Green are both rested for the Clippers clash.
And Cristiano Ronaldo rolled back the years! A 15-minute second-half hat-trick with goals in the 66th, 72nd, and 81st minutes to fire Al Nassr past Al Kholood 5-3.
Around the grounds. Afghanistan stunned Australia by four wickets in Mong Kok to claim the Hong Kong Sixes Cup final.
And in the Premier League, Manchester City were beaten 1-0 at home by Brighton.
